questions.question: What was the simple average day-ahead price at SPP's North hub in September 2026 (the local calendar month), in USD per MWh?
questions.answer:
The simple average day-ahead price at SPP's North hub (SPPNORTH_HUB) for September 2026 was 36.21 USD/MWh. This is the flat-load simple mean of 720 day-ahead hours, which is the full local month (cost_of_power_monthly, derived). The month is in Central time (America/Chicago).

The raw hourly table, iso_dam_hub_prices, holds only part of September for this hub. Its 301 hours run from 11 am Central on 18 September to 11 pm Central on 30 September. Their mean was 32.34 USD/MWh, but that covers only part of the month, so it is not the monthly figure.

questions.question: What was the mean day-ahead clearing price of ERCOT's Regulation Up service in September 2026 (the Central-time month), in USD per MW per hour?
questions.answer: ERCOT's Regulation Up (ercot:REGUP) day-ahead market clearing price for capacity (MCPC) averaged 1.84 USD/MW-hour in September 2026 (ercot_as_prices_monthly, derived). The figure is the mean over 720 hourly prices, which is all 720 hours of the month, so no hours are missing. It is a capacity price in USD/MW-hour, not an energy price. The monthly rollup is labelled with the Central-time month (September 1 to 30).

questions.question: Which calendar month of 2025 (Central time) had the highest single 15-minute real-time price at ERCOT's hub average, and what was that price, in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: April 2025 (Central time) had the highest single 15-minute real-time price at ERCOT's hub average (ercot:HB_HUBAVG). The maximum was 3553.1 USD/MWh (ercot_peak_premium_monthly, derived). The figure is the monthly maximum over 2880 fifteen-minute real-time intervals (all_max and n_intervals, same table). The next-highest months were May 2025 at 2350.31 USD/MWh and July 2025 at 1754.38 USD/MWh (same table).

questions.question: How many 15-minute real-time intervals at ERCOT's hub average had a price at or below zero from January to September 2026 (the nine Central-time months summed)?
questions.answer: 609 fifteen-minute real-time intervals at ERCOT's HB_HUBAVG had a price at or below zero from January to September 2026. This is the sum of the n_negative counts for the nine Central-time months (ercot_peak_premium_monthly, derived table, built from ERCOT's 15-minute real-time prices). Those nine months hold 26204 intervals in total (n_intervals, same table). September 2026 contributed 0 of the 609.

questions.question: In September 2026, how much higher or lower was the simple average day-ahead price at ERCOT's hub average than at CAISO's SP15 hub, in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: ERCOT's hub average was about 1.97 USD/MWh lower than CAISO's SP15 hub in September 2026 (cost_of_power_monthly, derived). The ERCOT HB_HUBAVG simple mean day-ahead price was 38.80 USD/MWh. The CAISO TH_SP15_GEN-APND simple mean was 40.77 USD/MWh. The difference, ERCOT minus CAISO, is -1.97 USD/MWh (compare). The month is local time, and each hub's month holds 720 day-ahead hours, so it is complete. Each figure is the unweighted mean of hourly day-ahead prices, with no demand weighting.

questions.question: On which operating day of September 2026 was the daily indicative spark spread at CAISO's SP15 hub (day-ahead daily mean less 7.0 MMBtu/MWh times Henry Hub) lowest, and what was it, in USD per MWh?
questions.answer: The daily spark spread at CAISO's SP15 hub (TH_SP15_GEN-APND) was lowest on 3 September 2026, at 8.51 USD/MWh (price_board_spreads, derived). It is the minimum of the 30 September daily values. The spark spread is the day-ahead daily mean less an assumed 7.0 MMBtu/MWh times Henry Hub. That day's day-ahead daily mean was 29.16 USD/MWh and its implied heat rate was 9.884 MMBtu/MWh (price_board_spreads). The day is the local operating day, labelled by its date at 00:00Z.
